title: ZIA Insights chart settings: units, chart types, top-N, filters, history and the data types that appear only on an Insights page

prose.label: Units.
prose.text: {{units-metrics-time}} The Web data types page offers time on more data types than this {{divergence:time-unit-scope}}. {{widget-units}} {{per-type-units}}

prose.label: Chart types and top items.
prose.text: {{chart-types}} {{top-n}} {{no-trend-chart}} How many items a widget shows is in [[zia.insights.dashboards]].

prose.label: Data types that appear only on an Insights page.
prose.text: {{insights-only-firewall-dns}} {{insights-only-web}} {{pqc-buckets}} The Endpoint DLP and Email DLP Insights-only data types are not named {{gap:edlp-insights-only-types}}, and whether Mobile and Extranet have any is not said {{gap:mobile-extranet-insights-only}}.

checks.do: Whether a data type is available in a widget or only on the Insights page before building a dashboard around it.
Whether a data type supports a trend chart, and which units it offers, before choosing it.
Whether a filter list is complete, since the User, Department and Location filters list 200 results at a time on the pages that say so.

two-ways.statement: The Web, Mobile, Firewall, DNS, Endpoint DLP, Email DLP and Extranet data types and filters pages each say their data types and filters are used in a dashboard or report widget or on an Insights page; The Web, Firewall, DNS, Endpoint DLP and Email DLP pages add that some data types appear only on the Insights page, not in the New Widget window.

quotes: There are two ways you work with web data types and filters to define the web traffic information that you want to view: in a dashboard or report widget, or when analyzing charts on an Insights page.
Certain data types only appear on the Web Insights page and not on the Dashboard > New Widget window.

There are two ways you work with mobile data types and filters to define the mobile traffic information that you want to view: in a dashboard or report widget, or when analyzing charts on an Insights page.

There are two ways you work with Firewall data types and filters to define the Firewall traffic information that you want to view: in a dashboard or report widget, or when analyzing charts on an Insights page.
Certain data types only appear on the Firewall Insights page and not on the Dashboard > New Widget window.
There are two ways you work with DNS data types and filters to define the web traffic information that you want to view: in a dashboard or report widget, or when analyzing charts on an Insights page.
Certain data types only appear on the DNS Insights page and not on the Dashboard > New Widget window.

There are two ways you can use Zscaler Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) data types and filters to define the Endpoint DLP activities information that you want to view: in a dashboard or report widget, or when analyzing charts on an Insights page.
Certain data types only appear on the Endpoint DLP Insights page and not on the Dashboard > New Widget window.

There are two ways you can use Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP) data types and filters to define the Email DLP activities information that you want to view: in a dashboard or report widget, or when analyzing charts on an Insights page.
Certain data types only appear on the Email DLP Insights page and not on the Dashboard > New Widget window.

There are two ways you work with Extranet data types and filters to define extranet traffic information that you want to view: in a dashboard or report widget, or when analyzing charts on an Insights page.

default-chart.statement: The default Web Insights page is a trend chart of the Overall Traffic data type for the current day, in transactions; a data type works as the "grouped by" of the chart.

quotes: This is what the default Web Insights page looks like.
It shows a trend chart for the data type Overall Traffic.
The chart shows the overall traffic for the current day in terms of transactions.
Think of data types as the "Grouped by..." section

custom-92.statement: On an Insights page a custom time frame can end up to 92 days after its start date, and a multi-day time frame shows the sum of bytes or transactions per day in the chosen chart type.

quotes: In Custom, the end date can be up to 92 days from the start date.
Selecting multiple days as a time frame results in seeing the sum of bytes/transactions per day in whichever chart type you select.

local-time.statement: Chart data is aggregated on the viewing administrator's local time, except trend charts; for example Current Day covers 12:00 AM to 11:59 PM local time.

quotes: Data in charts are aggregated based on the local time of the administrator, except for trend charts.
For example, data for Current Day will be summarized from 12:00 AM to 11:59 PM local time for the administrator viewing the report.

units-metrics-time.statement: The About Insights article says chart data is viewed as Units, as Metrics in Tunnel Insights only, and as Time for the Domain and URL Host data types only.

quotes: View the data as Units, Metrics (in Tunnel Insights only), and Time (for Domain and URL Host only).

widget-units.statement: A widget's unit is Transactions or Bytes; Samples are used only with the Secure Browsing Class, Status and Type data types, and bps only with Bandwidth by Department, by Location, by Location Groups, by Rule, Bandwidth Class and Bandwidth Consumption. View Logs is not offered on charts of secure browsing class, data or status because they use samples.

quotes: From the drop-down menu, choose Transactions or Bytes as the unit of data.
Samples are used only with the Secure Browsing Class, Secure Browsing Status, and Secure Browsing Type data types.
bps are used only with Bandwidth by Department, Bandwidth by Location, Bandwidth by Location Groups, Bandwidth by Rule, Bandwidth Class, and Bandwidth Consumption data types.
The View Logs option isn't available for charts that display secure browsing class, data, or status, because they only use samples as their data units.
This option is not available for charts that display secure browsing class, data or status, because they only use samples as their data units.

per-type-units.statement: Firewall and DNS Action data can be viewed as sessions or bytes; the Web data type for HTTP POST requests uses only the unit Bytes; Bandwidth Class shows bits per second; a 7-day bandwidth consumption trend chart can drill down to a 5-minute view.

quotes: Displays data about the action that the service took on your organization's traffic. You can view either the number of sessions or bytes.
Displays data about the action that the service took on your organization's traffic. You can view either the number of sessions or bytes.
POST requests include email that was sent through webmail or posted on a social networking site or blog. This data type uses only the unit Bytes.
Displays bandwidth usage in bits-per-second (bps) for each bandwidth class.
Displays a 7-day view of your organization's bandwidth usage in a trend chart. You can drill down to a 5-minute view.

chart-types.statement: Widgets and the Web, Mobile, Firewall, DNS and Tunnel Insights charts offer pie, bar, line, value and table charts.

quotes: When you edit a widget in a dashboard or report, or analyze a chart in Web Insights, Mobile Insights, Firewall Insights, DNS Insights, or Tunnel Insights, you can choose to display the following types of charts:
Pie Chart - Bar Chart - Line Chart - Value Chart - Table Chart

top-n.statement: For certain data types an Insights bar chart or table can show the top 5, 10, 25, 50 or 100 items; trend and pie charts show only the top 5, with the rest grouped as Other.

quotes: For certain data types, you can choose to view the top 5, 10, 25, 50 or 100 items.
This option is available in bar charts and tables only.
In trend and pie charts, you'll only see the top 5 items. The Other category refers to the rest of the data types not in the top 5.

no-trend-chart.statement: Among the data types that cannot be used with a trend chart are, on the Web page, the data types for user, URL category, instant messaging, detected viruses or spyware, webmail and a data type that only uses samples; on the Mobile page, application category and user; on the Endpoint DLP and Email DLP pages, document type and user.

quotes: Displays web traffic data organized by user. The trend chart does not support this data type.
Displays web traffic data grouped by URL category. The trend chart does not support this data type.
Displays data about the web traffic of instant messaging applications. The trend chart does not support this data type.
Displays data about detected viruses or spyware. The trend chart does not support this data type.
Displays data about webmail traffic. The trend chart does not support this data type.
It only uses samples as its data unit. This data type cannot be used with a trend chart.
Displays mobile traffic data grouped by application category. This data type cannot be used with a trend chart.
Displays mobile traffic data organized by user. The trend chart does not support this data type.
Displays Endpoint DLP data associated with document type. This data type cannot be used with a trend chart.
Displays Endpoint DLP data associated with users. The trend chart does not support this data type.
Displays Email DLP data associated with document type. This data type cannot be used with a trend chart.
Displays Email DLP data associated with users. The trend chart does not support this data type.

filters-200-values.statement: Multi-value filters such as Users, Departments and Locations take up to 200 values in one filter and can include or exclude them; as an example, the Department and Location filters don't appear together in Insights but do in Insights Logs.

quotes: Certain filters, like Users, Departments, Locations, and others, support the selection of multiple values. For these, you can select up to 200 values in a single filter. You can also choose to include or exclude the selected values.
For example, the Department and Location filters don't appear together in Insights, but appear together in Insights Logs when applied.

filter-lists-200.statement: On the Web and Mobile data types pages the User, Department and Location filters list 200 results at a time; the Endpoint DLP and Email DLP pages say this of the User and Department filters, and the Tunnel page of the Location filter.

quotes: The User, Department, and Location filters list 200 results at a time.
The User, Department, and Location filters list 200 results at a time.
The User and Department filters list 200 results at a time.
The User and Department filters list 200 results at a time.
The Location filter lists 200 results at a time.

history-bar.statement: The history bar keeps up to 50 versions of the chart and deletes the oldest beyond that; changing an earlier version deletes all later ones. Start Over returns to the default chart with the data type menu on Overall Traffic, filters reset and every chart but the default deleted from the history bar, and choosing a different data type resets the filters.

quotes: The history bar can retain up to 50 versions of the chart.
If there are more than 50 versions, the portal deletes the oldest versions as new ones are added.
If you view an earlier version and change it, all subsequent versions are automatically deleted.
Click Start Over to go back to the default chart.
The data type menu above the chart is set to Overall Traffic, filters are reset, and all charts, except the default, are deleted from the history bar.
Choose a different data type from the menu at the top. This automatically resets the filters.

insights-only-firewall-dns.statement: Firewall data types that appear only on the Firewall Insights page are Client Source IP, Client Tunnel IP, Server Destination IP and Threat Name; among the DNS data types that appear only on the DNS Insights page is one for the client IP address, and another for a destination server has no pie chart or trend line.

quotes: The following are the firewall data types that only appear on the Firewall Insights page:
Client Source IP
Client Tunnel IP
Server Destination IP
Threat Name
evidence.after: The following are the firewall data types that only appear on the Firewall Insights page:

quotes: Displays data on the traffic associated with a specific client IP address.
Displays data about traffic associated with a destination server. The pie chart and trend line are unavailable for this data type.
evidence.after: The following are the DNS data types that only appear on the DNS Insights page:

insights-only-web.statement: Among the web data types that appear only on the Web Insights page are ones for the internet gateway location IP addresses, source IP address information and an associated destination server (each viewable by number of transactions, bytes or time), ones grouped by domain and by host (with a Time unit for the duration spent on each URL), and PQC data types comparing PQC with classical key exchange and ranking client-side negotiated PQC or Hybrid key exchange algorithms and the users who could negotiate them.

quotes: Displays information on the internet gateway location IP addresses. You can view this information by number of transactions, bytes, or time.

Displays source IP address information, either the internet gateway location IP address or the IP address of the client device. You can view this information by number of transactions, bytes, or time.
Displays data grouped by domain. The unit Time appears, and you can select it to view the duration of time spent on each URL.
Displays a comparison between (Post-Quantum Cryptography) PQC vs. classical key exchange for web traffic.
Displays information associated with a destination server. You can view this information by number of transactions, bytes, or time.
Displays client-side negotiated PQC or Hybrid key exchange algorithms, ranked by their frequency.
Displays users who could negotiate PQC or Hybrid key exchange algorithms, ranking them by their transaction count.
Displays web traffic data grouped by host. The unit Time appears, and you can select it to view the duration of time spent on each URL.
evidence.after: The following are the web data types that only appear on the Web Insights page:

pqc-buckets.statement: In the PQC vs. Classical Key Exchange data type, Classical covers transactions whose client key exchange is Classical or Unknown, and PQC those whose client key exchange is PQC or Hybrid.

quotes: Classical: Click to view all transactions where the Client Key Exchange filter has either Classical or Unknown type set.
PQC: Click to view all transactions where the Client Key Exchange has either PQC or the Hybrid type set.

tunnel-data-types.statement: Tunnel Insights charts are filtered by Location (default All), Location Group (default None), Tunnel Destination IP, Tunnel Source IP, Tunnel Type (All, GRE or IPSec) and VPN Credential (default All).

quotes: Location: Use this filter to view metrics associated with a specific location. The default option for this filter is All.
Location Group: Use this filter to view metrics associated with a specific location group. The default option for this filter is None.
Tunnel Destination IP: Use this filter to view metrics associated with a destination IP address.
Tunnel Source IP: Use this filter to view metrics associated with a source IP address.
Tunnel Type: Use this filter to view metrics based on different types of tunnels.
All - GRE - IPSec
VPN Credential: Use this filter to view metrics associated with a specific VPN credential. The default option for this filter is All.

user-reports.statement: With User as the Web Insights data type the page lists top users, and Export All Active Users exports the active users to CSV; user reports include locations by default, which widgets can exclude.

quotes: Select User as the data type to list the top users.
You can also click Export All Active Users to export the list of active users to a CSV file.
By default, user reports also include locations. You can exclude locations in user reports by creating new or editing existing widgets.

browsing-time.statement: The time-based Web Insights report adds a user's time on the internet across all tabs and devices in the filtered period, covers the last seven days only, and can be inflated by traffic such as scripts and servers throttling update pushes.

quotes: Zscaler calculates the user's browsing time by adding the overall time spend on the internet across all tabs and devices within the filtered time period.
Other factors such as traffic running via scripts, throttling by servers when pushing updates, etc. contribute to an inflated time spend data.
This report provides data for the last seven days only.

time-unit-scope.summary: About Insights offers the Time unit for the Domain and URL Host data types only, while the Web data types page also offers time on the data types for gateway location IP addresses and a destination server.

quotes: View the data as Units, Metrics (in Tunnel Insights only), and Time (for Domain and URL Host only).

positions.says: Time is available for Domain and URL Host only.

quotes: Displays information on the internet gateway location IP addresses. You can view this information by number of transactions, bytes, or time.
Displays information associated with a destination server. You can view this information by number of transactions, bytes, or time.

positions.says: The data types for gateway location IP addresses and for a destination server can be viewed by transactions, bytes or time.

time-unit-scope.impact: Which data types offer the Time unit depends on which page is read; the pages do not say which is complete.

edlp-insights-only-types.title: Which Endpoint DLP and Email DLP data types appear only on the Insights page
edlp-insights-only-types.detail: The Endpoint DLP and Email DLP data types pages say some data types appear only on the Insights page, then list only the data types and filters that appear in both places. The Insights-only types are not named.

mobile-extranet-insights-only.title: Whether Mobile or Extranet have Insights-only data types
mobile-extranet-insights-only.detail: The Mobile and Extranet data types pages do not say whether any data type appears only on the Insights page.
